Record of Navigator decisions and Opus rejections. Only add to this file. Each entry has the date, the unit, the decision and the reason.

## 2026-11-10 — PLT-01 — how the Angular, NestJS and Zod majors are pinned (Option B)

- **Decision (Navigator):** Option B. PLT-01 records the Angular, NestJS and Zod majors in a documented pin section in the root `package.json`, and installs none of the three packages. The resolved numbers are recorded when PLT-01 is implemented, not hardcoded in the plan. PLT-02 adds `zod` to `packages/contracts`, PLT-03 adds `@angular/*` and Material to `apps/web`, and PLT-04 adds `@nestjs/core` and `@nestjs/serve-static` to `apps/api`, each at its recorded major. The pin is a section, not npm `overrides`.
- **Reason (Navigator):** Keeps the three packages out of the lockfile until their owning units. Avoids baking possibly stale version numbers into a plan that is not implemented in this iteration.
- **Driver challenge (open at the time of writing):** The stated reason "no downstream file changes" does not separate Option A from Option B. Under both, PLT-02, PLT-03 and PLT-04 edit the workspace `package.json` files that PLT-01 creates (PLT-01 Scope line 32). No acceptance criterion tests the pin section (AC 4 covers only Node and npm). The challenge is recorded in a separate navigator question. Its answer will be added here.

- **Decision (Navigator):** Option (a). Keep Option B. - **Driver note:** The challenge recorded in the entry above is closed by this answer.

## 2026-11-10 — PLT-01 — TypeScript major in the pin section

- **Decision (Navigator, confirmed):** TypeScript is pinned to the 6.0.x line (range `>=6.0 <6.1`). The exact patch is resolved when PLT-01 is implemented and recorded in the root `package.json` pin section. 7.x and 5.x are rejected. The earlier "6.x" label is withdrawn as too wide.
- **Reason (Navigator, checked by the driver against the npm registry, 2026-11-10):** `@angular/build@22.2.5`, `@angular-devkit/build-angular@22.2.5` and `@angular/compiler-cli@22.2.5` each declare peer `typescript` `>=6.0 <6.1`, which alone forces 6.0.x. The registry `latest` is 7.0.2, which those packages exclude. Angular 21 accepts `>=5.9 <6.0` and Angular 20 accepts `>=5.8 <6.0`, so no Angular line checked accepts 7.x. `typescript-eslint` (latest) declares `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`, a secondary constraint not required by the PLT-01 unit.
- **Why the newest-major rule does not apply to TypeScript:** the rule was set for Angular, NestJS and Zod. Applied to TypeScript it picks 7.0.2, which the Angular build tooling excludes.

## 2026-11-10 — PLT-01 — Node runtime for the tests

- **Decision (Navigator):** The Node pin is Node 26 in `.nvmrc` and `engines`, as PLT-01 Decisions line 25 requires. This iteration writes `plans/PLT-01.md` with `status: planned` only and runs no tests. No local Node 24.21.0 run is recorded, and no criterion is marked passed. ## 2026-11-10 — PLT-01 — location and coverage of the pin-section test

- **Decision (Navigator):** The test for the new pin-section criterion is `scripts/pins.test.mjs` at the repo root. It runs with Node's built-in `node:test`, invoked by the root `test` script after the workspace fan-out. It asserts that the keys `angular`, `nestjs` and `zod` are present in the root pin section. It does not check version numbers, and it has no TypeScript key.
- **Reason (Navigator):** The pin section is in the root `package.json`, so the test is root-owned. `packages/contracts` belongs to PLT-02, so the test is not placed there. A root Vitest config would add a file and a dependency for a presence check. `node:test` is built into Node, and the root `test` script already fans out to every workspace. The criterion names only the three majors, so the coverage matches it.
- **Correction:** The Navigator's reason "a TypeScript key would force version checking" is wrong. A presence check on a TypeScript key does not check its version. The coverage choice still stands, because the criterion names only the three majors, and widening the criterion is the Navigator's call.

## 2026-11-10 — PLT-01 — Opus rejection 2 of the plan (blocking problem)

- **Rejection (Opus subagent, re-review of revision 2):** `plans/PLT-01.md` is not approved. Count for PLT-01: 2 rejections. The next rejection is the third, and at three the Navigator must choose to make the unit smaller, divide it, or stop it.
- **Blocking:** The `.prettierignore` entries in revision 2 are unanchored (`modules/`). Gitignore rules make such a pattern match a folder of that name at any depth, so `apps/api/src/modules/**` would be ignored too. The driver confirmed this with Prettier 3: `apps/api/src/modules/platform/platform.module.ts` reports `"ignored": true` with `modules/`, and `"ignored": false` with `/modules/`.
- **Non-blocking, folded into the revision:** PLT-03's replacement `package.json` must keep `build`, `test` and `lint` scripts. PLT-09's fixtures must fail lint, so the root config needs an ignore for their folder. PLT-13 also adds a root `e2e` script. PLT-11 adds a root `README.md` that Prettier checks. Prettier formatting is applied to `package.json` before the check. The unit branch `unit/PLT-01` is created before the first commit, and the fresh clone uses `-b unit/PLT-01`. The chosen Angular major's build peer must admit the 6.0 patch. The `packageManager` value must match an exact npm version.

## 2026-11-10 — PLT-01 — Opus rejection 3 of the plan (blocking problem)

- **Rejection (Opus subagent, round 3 review of revision 3):** `plans/PLT-01.md` is not approved. Count for PLT-01: 3 rejections. Per the driver rules, at three rejections the Navigator must select one of: make the unit smaller, divide the unit, or stop the unit. No further plan revision is made before that selection.
- **Blocking:** The workspace `package.json` files have no `version`. npm prints the package name in each workspace's run banner only when `version` is set. The driver confirmed this in a temporary two-workspace project: the workspace without `version` printed `> build`, and the one with `"version": "0.0.0"` printed `> @x/b@0.0.0 build`. So AC 2's requirement that each fan-out name all four packages cannot be met as written. The fix is `"version": "0.0.0"` in each workspace, plus a banner check in AC 2.
- **Non-blocking, to fold in if the unit continues:** Step 1 must resolve the tool versions and require `npm install` to succeed without `--legacy-peer-deps`. Step 1c must check the exact Angular version from step 1a, and also the `@angular/compiler-cli` peer. Step 3 must run AC 2 to 5 in the working tree, with AC 1 run after the step 4 commit. Step 2 must run `prettier --write` after the install, so the locked Prettier version formats the files. Section 5 must cover the TypeScript devDependency that the Angular and NestJS generators add, the root Prettier check reaching the files PLT-03, PLT-10 and PLT-12 add, PLT-12's tests not running under root `npm test` if `e2e/` stays a plain folder, and any root devDependency PLT-09 adds. The smoke test must import `describe`, `it` and `expect` from `vitest`.

## 2026-11-10 — PLT-01 — response to the third rejection (Navigator decision)

- **Decision (Navigator):** Keep PLT-01 as one unit and fix the defects in place. No scope cut, no division, no stop. Apply the blocking fix (`"version": "0.0.0"` in each of the four workspace `package.json` files, plus a banner check that npm names all four packages in AC 2) and the non-blocking notes above. Then re-send the plan to Opus.

The driver records the selection as keep-whole, fix-in-place. This is not one of the three literal options. It is flagged here so the user can see it.

## 2026-11-10 — PLT-01 — Angular and TypeScript conflict rule (Navigator decision)

- **Decision (Navigator):** Option (a). The newest-Angular-major rule and the TypeScript 6.0.x line are two separate Navigator decisions. If the newest Angular major's build-tooling TypeScript peer excludes the 6.0.x line, the implementation stops and records the conflict for the Navigator. It does not pick a non-newest Angular major, and it does not move the TypeScript line.
- **Reason (Navigator):** Choosing an older Angular major would silently downgrade a decision. Moving the TypeScript line would silently reopen the 6.0.x decision, whose premise is the Angular 22.2.5 build peer. Only the Navigator may re-decide either one.

## 2026-11-13 — PLT-16 — Finding during the smoke run: the late-login premise of ST-1 fails under the shipped compose (evidence; not a decision)

- **Evidence (Opus code review of `c75948c`, reproduced by the coordinator with read-only commands on the `plt16-check` stack):** with no auth key, containerboot's `tailscale up` times out after about 60 s and the sidecar exits. Docker restarts it: `RestartCount` 8 at 05:07 UTC. Each restart prints a new login URL, so a URL handed over at step 11 is replaced within about a minute. The sidecar's log shows the new `AuthURL` at each start (the URL itself is not recorded here).
- **Effect on `scriba`:** `scriba` runs with `network_mode: service:tailscale`, and it was never restarted (`StartedAt` 04:59:01 UTC). Its network namespace belongs to the earlier sidecar instance. At 05:07 UTC the host `/healthz` on port 18080 returns 000. Inside `scriba`, the route table is empty and the `host.docker.internal` fetch fails with ENETUNREACH, while `scriba`'s own healthcheck still reports healthy.
- **What this means for the plan:** ST-1 (unit line 21) says "start compose with no auth key, app healthy on loopback; log in later via the auth URL". Under the shipped compose, a later login cannot reach Serve. The served app is unreachable after any restart of the sidecar, and a person cannot approve a URL that is gone within a minute. The N1 approval step is therefore not achievable as the plan describes it.
- **Steps 7 to 9 stay valid:** they ran in the first window (steps 7 and 8 between 04:59:01 and 05:00:01 UTC; step 8 at 04:59:27 to 04:59:38). Step 9's exact time is not logged.

- **Decision:** the ST-1 late-login half is recorded as FAILED under the shipped compose. It is a failure, not a deferral: the flow was run and broke. Criterion 1 (unit line 27) stays unticked, with the cause. The PLT-16 batch waits. The compose fix is a separate change (a PLT-15 revision or a new unit). Merging PLT-16 without criterion 1 is a separate later decision. Do not merge now.
- **Cause (reproduced by the coordinator, read-only):** with no auth key, `tailscale up` times out after about 60 s and the sidecar exits; Docker restarts it (RestartCount 8), and each restart prints a new login URL, so a URL handed over at step 11 is dead within about a minute. `scriba` (`network_mode: service:tailscale`) was never restarted, so its namespace belongs to the old sidecar instance, and host `/healthz` on port 18080 returns 000. Both contradict unit line 21: "log in later via the auth URL … still does after `docker compose restart`".
- **Why not (b) or (c):** (b) changes the compose file, which is PLT-15's approved deliverable (reopening it as a side effect of a smoke test would conflate verification with a product change). (c) changes what criterion 1 tests, which only the Navigator may do, and it would weaken the criterion (prompt.md line 146).
- **Consequences:** the ADR's Attempt A records the late-login failure with this evidence, and its `Shipped variant` line stays open until the compose fix is re-tested. Criteria 2 to 4 keep the earlier decisions N2 to N5 (N2 reboot deferred; N3 Linux leg deferred; N5 2c deferred). N1 (the person's login approval) cannot complete while the URL is ephemeral.
- **Downstream effect:** `phase:smoke` (PLT-16) stays open, so PLT-17 and SAU-21 stay blocked (unit lines 9 and 14 of PLT-16).

## 2026-11-13 — SHL-01 / SHL-02 / SHL-03 — zod in the browser bundle: the Shell ships no runtime zod (Navigator decision, option c; session 17b006e4a2bb4441868aca77bff75496)

- **Decision (Navigator):** the Shell (SHL-02, SHL-03, SHL-04) ships no runtime zod. All contracts imports in the Shell are type-only, and type imports are erased at build. Runtime validation uses hand-written guards: `isPlatformErrorBody` for error bodies (SHL-02, decision 6) and an `isPlatformEnvelope` guard for the SSE envelope (SHL-03). A Vitest parity test runs each guard against the contracts schemas in Node, where the CommonJS build is fine.
- **No budget change:** `apps/web/angular.json` stays as it is (warning 500 kB, error 1 MB). The default build keeps no `allowedCommonJsDependencies` entry. Only `contracts-boot` has one (line 55).
- **SHL-08:** its runtime setup-auth schema is loaded by SHL-08 itself: a dynamic import in its own chunk, or a dedicated build configuration with `allowedCommonJsDependencies` as `contracts-boot` has. The Shell batch does not preload it. SHL-08's plan decides this when it is written.
- **Reasons:** (1) consistency: SHL-02 decision 5 already took this route, and PLT-11 (DECISIONS line 631) kept contracts and zod out of the production bundle. (2) Cost: a runtime import of `/platform` adds about 564 kB of zod's CommonJS build (DECISIONS line 634); the initial bundle would be about 886 kB, above the 500 kB warning. (3) A dynamic import (SHL-03 option a) only moves the 564 kB to a startup chunk, and the default build still lacks the CommonJS allowance. (4) Raising the budget is a one-way change that every later feature inherits.
- **Consequences for the drafts:** `plans/SHL-03.md` open point 1 (line 175) flips from the static import to this route. Its eager `/platform` import becomes `import type`, with the hand-written `isPlatformEnvelope` guard and the parity test; open point 6 (CommonJS warnings) is closed, because the default build needs no allowance. `plans/SHL-02.md` open point 1 (line 143) is closed by this entry; decision 5 is unchanged.
- **Note:** SHL-01's open point 1 ("for the Navigator, before SHL-02") is answered by this entry.

## 2026-11-13 — SHL-03 — Opus code review of `unit/SHL-03` (head 402e9bc, base main 3345bfe): NOT APPROVED (rejection 1 of the code)

- **Result (Opus subagent, fresh context):** NOT APPROVED. One blocking problem, and the fix stays inside the plan's files and the text of decision 9.
  1. [blocking] Criterion 3 and decision 9: the backoff does not grow when a recovered stream closes again before it opens. `recover()` in `sse-client.ts` adds to `failures` only when a probe fails or returns 401; when both probes pass it calls `connect('reconnecting')` and adds nothing. If that stream reaches CLOSED without opening, the next wait uses the same n. The reviewer's scratch spec gave EventSources at 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000 and 6000 ms: a fixed 1 s loop of three requests per cycle (healthz, status, events) that never reaches the 30 s cap. Decision 9 counts "failed recoveries since the last open", so a recovery whose stream never opened is a failed one. Correction: in `recover()`, add `this.failures += 1;` just before `this.connect('reconnecting')` (`handleOpen` already resets it to 0). Make T9 stricter in place (still 12 tests): after the second stream at 1 s, fire `emitError(2)` on it, advance 2 s, and assert that the third EventSource has `createdAt` 3000. The reviewer's scratch probe gives 0, 1000, 3000 with this fix, and all 12 tests pass.

## 2026-11-13 — SHL-06 — criterion 1 on the dev stack: option (b), a dev-only proxy hook (Navigator decision; session 57d851d74d62450ca9f7cab2d9b775ec)

- **Decision (Navigator, option b):** a dev-proxy `configure` hook destroys the client response when the upstream aborts, so the browser's EventSource fires its error and the existing CONNECTING path runs on the dev stack. Criterion 1's wording (unit line 19) stands. Its verify note: the dev stack through the proxy hook, plus a one-time production stop check on the API-served build (single origin, native EventSource error).
- **Facts (checked):** the Vite 8.3.7 proxy pipes the upstream response into the client response with no abort handling (`node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js` line 19252), so after the API destroys the stream on shutdown (`apps/api/src/modules/platform/events/events.publisher.ts` lines 70 to 77) the browser's stream stays half-open. Production has no proxy: NestJS serves the bundle on one origin, and a process stop closes the TCP connection, so the EventSource error fires natively.
- **Rejected (a):** a heartbeat watchdog in `SseClient`. The 15 s heartbeat is a comment line (`events.publisher.ts` line 56), which the browser's EventSource does not expose; an envelope-only watchdog would reconnect a healthy quiet stream every ~30 s, against the "small, unobtrusive" indicator (unit line 15). A data-line heartbeat is a Platform protocol change (PLT-06): a one-way door, disproportionate to a dev-demo gap.
- **Rejected (c):** judging criterion 1 on the API-served build only. SHL-09's demo step 5 needs the same behaviour on `npm run dev`.
- **Consequence for the files:** the hook is dev-only local code with no external request, so PLT-03's offline rationale is unchanged. It needs a proxy config that can carry a hook: the change is for the SHL-06 plan (to be revised), not for PLT-03's merged code by itself.

## 2026-11-13 — SHL-05 — gated URL: the larger-screen page renders in place (Navigator decision; session 57d851d74d62450ca9f7cab2d9b775ec)

- **Decision (Navigator, option a):** a phone that opens a gated URL keeps the URL it asked for, and the "needs a larger screen" page renders there. The gate's `canMatch` returns false on a phone, so the gated route does not match and a fallback renders at the same URL. The page has an in-page link back to a useful destination (home or the project list). The browser back button returns to the previous page, with no redirect loop. The draft's redirect to `/larger-screen` (`plans/SHL-05.md` decision 7) is replaced by this.
- **Reason:** the unit (`units/SHL-05-breakpoint-gate-nav.md` line 19) says "opening it directly shows a 'needs a larger screen' page with a link back"; criterion line 25 says "opening its URL on a phone viewport shows the 'larger screen' page". Neither requires a URL change. `canMatch` returning false is the idiomatic reading of `modules/shell.md` line 63. A redirect would make the back button loop (back, gated URL, redirect, back). Preserving the URL also means a rotation or resize up shows the real page without a second navigation.
- **Constraint for the design (added here):** the fallback must not catch unknown URLs, which keep the NotFound page (SHL-01 decision 8). The fallback is therefore one generated sibling per gated entry, with the same path and a `canMatch` that is true only when the device is below the entry's minimum; this is generated by `withDeviceGate`, not written into the route table.
- **Correction to a citation in the entry above (d2a3a4f):** the AGL-07 docked-slot wording is at `units/AGL-07-chat-panel-ui.md` line 17 (its first Decisions bullet), not line 8 (line 8 is `parallel_with`).

## 2026-11-13 — SAU-04 — Revision 2 addition to `plans/SAU-04.md`: malformed `SCRIBA_DEV_ORIGINS` refused at boot (decision 7)

## 2026-11-13 — SAU-04 — Navigator decision: the Host check and CSP run before the body parser (revision 1 rejection, items 2 and 5)

- **Decision (Navigator, session `7bd39660cbee4380bf275ec4c4e1de9d`, answer to the parser question):** the Host check and the `Content-Security-Policy` header run before the body parser. Mechanism a1: `app.use(...)` in `apps/api/src/bootstrap.ts` between `NestFactory.create` and `app.init()`. Scope i: registered only when `SetupAuthModule` is in the composed module list, so the ten Platform-only test apps (modules `[PlatformModule]`) do not change. The refusal (403 `AUTH_HOST_REJECTED`) and the CSP are written by the middleware itself, in Platform's base error shape.
- **Reason:** the body parser is registered in `NestApplication.init()` (`@nestjs/core` 12.4.2, `package/nest-application.js` line 127), not in `NestFactory.create`, so middleware added before `init()` runs first. A POST with a foreign Host and a malformed or oversize body then gets 403 `AUTH_HOST_REJECTED` with the CSP, not 400 or 413. Production always composes `SetupAuthModule`, so the security posture is the same under scope i and scope ii.
- **Corrections by the driver to the first answer:** that answer said the placement is a provider or an `httpServer` option. Both are wrong: `NestFactory.create` takes the adapter as its second argument and has no `httpServer` option (`package/nest-factory.js` lines 27 to 30); a provider's `onModuleInit` runs inside `init()`, after the parser; and the Platform test apps are not unaffected, because `createTestApp` listens on an ephemeral port (`apps/api/test/create-test-app.ts` line 57) that the allowlist refuses. These were recorded as rejected claims in the Navigator session.
- **Open for the plan (not decided here):** where the `SCRIBA_DEV_ORIGINS` validation runs, since the Host map is built before `app.use`. It must still refuse at boot with `BootError` (exit 1, a stderr line naming `SCRIBA_DEV_ORIGINS`). The planner decides, and records the decision in the plan.
- **Consequences for the SAU-04 plan (revision 3):** decisions 1, 11 and 15 and criteria 2 and 5 change. The Host check and the CSP are no longer Nest middleware. Decision 11 (errors from middleware reach Platform's filter) does not hold for an express-level middleware and must be checked before the plan says so.

## 2026-11-13 — SAU-04 — Navigator decision on the design point of revision 5: `redirect: false` for the static root (option a)

- **Decision (Navigator, session `7bd39660cbee4380bf275ec4c4e1de9d`):** add `serveStaticOptions: { redirect: false }` to the `ServeStaticModule.forRoot` call in `apps/api/src/app.module.ts`. The default redirect answers `GET /media` with a 301 whose `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` replaces the hook's `frame-ancestors 'none'` (`@nestjs/serve-static` 2.2.1 `index.js` line 203). An exception would make the invariant conditional for every later static change. A one-property change makes it total. The Platform file is in scope because it serves the guard's own invariant.

## 2026-11-13 — MPR-01 — Coordinator decisions D-a, D-b and D-c on the create body (the gaps Opus found after the Navigator's decision c1d4804)

- **D-a (at least one id source):** `providerCreateSchema` is refined so that the body carries `presetId` or `label`, or both. A body with neither is refused. Without this, a valid body had no id base (Opus review, DECISIONS entry "targeted review of the label change").
- **D-b (preset ids only):** `presetId` is `z.enum(PROVIDER_PRESET_IDS)`, where `PROVIDER_PRESET_IDS` is the tuple `ollama`, `lm-studio`, `openai`, `openrouter`. So `presetId: '!!!'` is refused. Before this, any non-empty string passed, and it could slug to an empty base.
- **D-c (ASCII slug rule):** the label is lowercased first. Then each run of characters other than a–z and 0–9 becomes one hyphen, and leading and trailing hyphens are trimmed. The label must contain at least one ASCII letter or digit (`/[A-Za-z0-9]/`), so the slug is never empty. Examples: "My Local Llama" gives `my-local-llama`; "Café 2" gives `caf-2`; "日本語 1" gives `1`; "!!!" is refused.
- **Why coordinator decisions:** each is a small choice that the unit and module do not settle, and each only tightens the Navigator's option (a) (c1d4804). None changes the Navigator's rule that the label is optional and not stored, and the id base is `presetId`, else the slug of `label`.
- **Process:** the plan cites this entry next to c1d4804. The text goes through a targeted Opus review before `status: planned`.

## 2026-11-13 — MPR-04 — coordinator decision on timeout 0, superseding DECISIONS line 1889 (entry "coordinator decisions on the drafts", f2260eb)

- **Supersedes line 1889.** Line 1889 says that a timeout of 0 runs no client timer and that the SDK's default bounds a silent wait. That is withdrawn. Its premise is wrong for chat streams: the SDK's timer is cleared once the headers arrive, and the built-in fetch (undici) caps a silent wait at 300 s.
- **Decision.** A `config.timeout` of 0 means a limit of **300 000 ms** (the client's own timer uses it, and the SDK receives the same value). A value above 300 000 is still enforced by the client's own timer, but undici ends a silent wait at 300 s first. The plan states that cap.
- **Errors.** Both undici timeout causes (`UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`, `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT`) and the SDK's `APIConnectionTimeoutError` map to PROVIDER_TIMEOUT. An SDK connection error that is not a timeout maps to PROVIDER_UNREACHABLE, as before.
- **Rejected.** Keep 600 000 and record the cap (option a): the plan would then describe a limit that the runtime never gives. The 300 000 value makes the stated limit and the runtime agree.
- **Driver's checks:** the undici copy at 8.12.4, `lib/dispatcher/client.js` 318 and 319 (both 300 000 ms); the openai 7.55.0 copy (`client.js` 1824 is the 600 000 default; `APIConnectionTimeoutError` in `core/error.js` 78 and 88); Node 26.13.0 bundles undici 8.12.2.

## 2026-11-13 — MPR-04 — coordinator decision on a stream that ends normally after the first chunk (abort or timer)

- **Decision.** When the SDK's stream iterator ends normally after the first chunk, the client first checks the caller's abort (PROVIDER_ABORTED) and then its own timer (PROVIDER_TIMEOUT). Only if neither fired does the finish rule of S9 apply. Reason: the SDK returns silently on an abort (`core/streaming.js` lines 136 to 139 and 499 to 514), so without this check a cut-off stream would be reported as `finish stop`.
- **Accepted gap.** The path where the client's timer fires after the first chunk and the SDK iterator ends silently has no test: the mock's `chunkDelayMs` applies before every delta. It is named as a mock gap (MPR-04 open point 8). The timer before the first byte is tested (criterion 5, D11).
- **Driver's checks:** the SDK copy (openai 7.55.0, `core/streaming.js` 136 to 141 and 499 to 514). The stream-end rule is recorded in `plans/MPR-04.md` (lines 49, 50, 52, 207).

## 2026-11-13 — MPR-04 — coordinator decision widened: a stream that ends normally, with or without chunks (widens the entry at DECISIONS line 1915)

- **Decision.** When the SDK's stream iterator ends normally, with or without chunks, the client first checks the caller's abort (PROVIDER_ABORTED) and then its own timer (PROVIDER_TIMEOUT, retried only if no chunk had arrived). Only if neither fired does the rest apply: no chunk at all is PROVIDER_BAD_RESPONSE (not retried); otherwise the finish rule of S9 applies.
- **Reason.** The SDK's signal combination returns the iterator silently when the caller's signal aborts, even before the first chunk (`core/streaming.js` 499 to 514; the signal is combined after the headers, `client.js` 1878 to 1891). Without the check, a user Stop while the model is still thinking would be reported as BAD_RESPONSE.
- **Accepted gap.** The window between the headers and the first chunk is not reproducible with the mock (it writes the head and the first chunk together, `server.mjs` 408 to 422). It is named as a mock gap (MPR-04 open point 8).
- **Driver's checks:** the SDK copy (openai 7.55.0) `core/streaming.js` 136 to 141 and 499 to 514; `client.js` 1878 to 1891.

## 2026-11-13 — MPR-04 — coordinator decisions on the Opus code review of unit/MPR-04 (NOT APPROVED; the defects are fixed in the code, not the plan)

- **An empty key is no key.** `target.key` of `''` is treated as absent: a keyless provider uses the placeholder, and a keyRef without a key gives PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED. Before, `''` reached the SDK constructor and escaped as an uncoded error (`openai-compatible-client.ts` lines 185 to 208). A test in D2 asserts it.
- **listModels validates the raw body.** A 200 reply that is not a model list (for example an HTML page from a wrong URL) is PROVIDER_BAD_RESPONSE, not an empty list. The SDK's page sets `data` to `[]` for any body, so the check reads the raw body (`client.get`) and requires `data` to be an array of objects with a string `id`. One test is added to the models file (D8b): a local server answers `text/html` with 200, and the client returns PROVIDER_BAD_RESPONSE. This adds one test to the 25 (the plan's section 4 count becomes 26).
- **Timer disarmed before a retry sleep.** The timer is disarmed (or the scope closed) before the backoff sleep, so a retry does not run under a stale timer.
- **Two tests tightened.** Criterion 6 asserts a single `events.next()` after the abort. D10 counts the events drained before the rejection and asserts at most one.
- **Commits.** The plan's step 15 names one commit; the code has four, one per part (the per-part rule). Accepted: the branch keeps four commits.
- **Driver's checks:** the Opus review's file and line citations (the empty-key path, the listModels guard at line 328, `core/pagination.js` 79 to 91); the SDK pagination lines read by the reviewer.

Change `deploy/compose.yaml` only if it does not. Reason: `docs/adr/0001-tailscale-serve-mechanism.md` line 43 says "Whether `depends_on` with `restart: true` covers this is not checked", and `plans/PLT-15.md` section 8 (line 398) lists the non-coverage as an assumption. The check is a runtime test in S-U1: kill the tailscaled process in `tailscale`, let Docker restart the container, and record whether `scriba` also restarts (its `StartedAt`) and whether the published port answers. If the gap is confirmed, the fix (a healthcheck or a watchdog) moves `deploy/compose.yaml` into the file list of `plans/PLT-18.md` section 2, and that change is planned and reviewed again before the code. If the gap is not confirmed, no compose change is made.
- **Note from the Navigator's findings (not a decision).** `depends_on` uses `condition: service_started`, not `service_healthy`; if a healthcheck is later added to `tailscale`, revisit the condition. The README's new text goes in one operations section, shared with the install, update and rollback text.
- **Consequence.** `plans/PLT-18.md` takes these two answers in section 6 (P3 closed, with the items above) and adds the S-U1 runtime step for item 2. The next Opus review checks the revision against this entry.

## 2026-11-14 — PLT-18 — the Navigator's decisions on P11 (the fast path), P4 (the E5 re-point), P5 (the pull fallback) and P8 (the order of S-U1)

- **P11, the fast path: (a).** The Navigator (session e441ef9487974df3be73d324870f7d76, `decide`, 2026-11-14): the README documents the limit. `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` moves the image only when `SCRIBA_IMAGE_TAG` names a moving tag (for example `latest`), or after a re-run has written a new release tag; pinned users update by re-running the one-liner. Reason: the pin exists for reproducibility and rollback; telling users to switch to `latest` (option b) would defeat that. The unit's wording "covers image-only releases" is narrowed by the README, and that narrowing is recorded here.
- **P4, the E5 re-point: (a).** The Navigator confirms that `installer-preflight.test.ts` lines 105 to 130 are re-pointed to E5. The test's invariant (nothing is written before the checks) is kept; only the stderr reason changes, from the `.env` refusal to the Docker check, because the Docker check now comes first. Reason: PLT-17 D7 and PLT-17 section 5 (d) name this re-point as PLT-18's. E5 is red on `main` until PLT-18 lands, where the `.env` refusal fires first; that red window is expected and is not a regression.
- **P5, the pull fallback: (a).** Keep `docker compose pull --ignore-pull-failures`. `up -d` is the real safety net: it fails if an image is absent. Reason: a tag built on this machine has no registry copy, and a plain pull would exit non-zero and abort the update for no reason. The README's update section says that a failed pull is printed and the run continues to `up -d`.
- **P8, the order of S-U1 and PLT-17's Mac run: (a).** Run S-U1 now. S-U1 builds `0.1.1`, reads `0.1.0` and uses port 18081; PLT-17's U4 uses `latest` and `0.1.0` on port 8080. There is no tag or port conflict, and PLT-17 is `done`; its U4 is a manual Mac-terminal limit, not a criterion or a gate.
- **Consequence.** `plans/PLT-18.md` closes P4, P5, P8 and P11 in section 6, with these decisions and the DECISIONS entry names. The README's new text includes the fast-path limit (P11) and the failed-pull sentence (P5). The code stage may start.

  1. S-P1's mode detection uses `docker inspect --format '{{.Id}}' "$(hostname)"`, which can match an image or a volume as well as a container. Use `docker inspect --type container` so a host whose hostname matches another object is not put in mode N.

  3. Cleanup leaves some Docker state behind (the S-P3 build cache in the default builder, and any base images S-P1 pulls). That is harmless; the plan says so.
- **Status.** Set to `planned` in a separate commit. The code stage starts in a later iteration; its Docker steps write only to temporary folders and remove them.

## 2026-11-14 — SHL-11 — the Navigator's decision on open decision 1 (raw HTML): the strict reading, via the preview component

- **Decision (Navigator session `60a02ed51f4c4776b59d549f16d2867b`, `set_plan`, 2026-11-14).** Raw HTML never renders as elements in the Markdown preview. The preview component provides `MARKED_OPTIONS` at component level, with a renderer that escapes `html` tokens, so raw `img`, `a`, `div` and HTML comments show as literal text. The sanitiser stays on and is never bypassed (SHL-01's decision 5 stands). `app.config.ts` is not changed, and no dependency is added (`marked` and `ngx-markdown` are present).
- **Reason.** The unit's wording (line 15: "never run scripts or raw HTML from files or agent output"; line 24: "nothing renders as active HTML") is broader than criterion 2's fixtures. Under the sanitiser alone, a raw `<img src>` from agent output is shown and requests its source when displayed (the plan's F10 measurements). The component-level provider keeps the change inside SHL-11's own files.
- **Condition.** The renderer fact (that `ngx-markdown` exports `MARKED_OPTIONS` and `MarkedRenderer`, and that a component-level provider takes effect) is unverified in the Navigator's record. The plan must prove it with a jsdom spec before it is final: raw `img`, `a`, `div` and a comment render as literal text, with no such element in the DOM and no request for the image.
- **Effects.** SHL-10's card renders Markdown through this preview, so its output escapes raw HTML too; if the card ever gets its own Markdown component, it must carry the same provider. CEX-02's word-count rule is unchanged (it already strips HTML comments before counting); a draft's HTML comment appears as literal text in the preview, which is acceptable. SHL-19's accessibility check is unaffected.
- **Still open.** Open decisions 2 (the front-matter rule) and 3 (jsdom as the local procedure).

The offering rule is `enabled` and `valid` (TRG-06 lines 22 and 25), so the palette (GRR-11 line 19) lists `enabled && valid`, and each name appears once.
  6. [Navigator] A defect: for an invalid user copy of a built-in, `GET /tools/:name` returns the built-in (the "effective spec"), and `/builtin` returns the built-in too, so no route reaches the copy's source, which the editor needs (TRG-14). The smallest rule, with no contract change, is that `GET /tools/:name` returns the user file whenever one exists, valid or not, and `/builtin` returns the built-in. The alternative is a thirteenth route, `/tools/:name/user`, which is an expand and can come later. The Navigator must choose.
  7. Smaller slips: the decision entries say "five unit files" where six are named; the TRG-01 unit's line 30 puts `error?` outside the summary braces, and "unreadable" should read "a file that cannot be parsed or is refused".

## 2026-11-14 — SHL-11 — the Navigator's decision on open decision 2 (the front-matter rule): option A

- **Decision (Navigator session `60a02ed51f4c4776b59d549f16d2867b`, `decide`, 2026-11-14).** The Shell's front-matter rule is Pandoc's block shape (optional BOM; a first line that is only `---`; the next line not blank; the first later line that is only `---` or `...` closes) with the YAML-shape regex guard (the first non-blank line between the fences is a `#` comment or looks like a mapping key) in place of a YAML parser.
- **Reason.** Options B and C each change five criterion-1 tests from shown to hidden: prose between two rules and scene breaks would be hidden, which the unit's purpose ("renders cleanly without raw front matter") does not ask for. Exact alignment with `readFrontMatter` also needs its YAML parse, so it needs a YAML library in `apps/web`, which the no-new-dependency rule forbids (`plans/DECISIONS.md` lines 1084 to 1089). Option A adds no dependency and keeps all nine criterion-1 tests as written.
- **Effects.** No criterion-1 test changes. Controls M5 and M8 keep their "shown" expectations. The notes go to CEX-02, CEX-04, PST-08, PST-10 and SHL-15 only (no criterion text changes): if an API-side rule is later planned and differs, the Shell's copy follows it by a later change.
- **Correction for CEX-04.** A subagent's read of CEX-04 inverted the prose-first case. `plans/SHL-11.md` line 24 is authoritative: under option A the Shell shows a prose-first block and a block that opens with a blank line, and Pandoc's stripping (CEX-04 lines 25 and 35) need not match.
- **Still open.** Open decision 3 (jsdom as the local procedure for "nothing executes"). The renderer fact (`MARKED_OPTIONS` at component level) must still be proven in a jsdom spec before the plan is final.

## 2026-11-15 — SAU-08 — PLAN DOES NOT WORK at step 7 (the e2e run, criterion 8 step (e)): the landing loads the CommonJS contract namespace in the production build

- **Report (implementer, branch `unit/SAU-08`):** step 7 fails at criterion 8 step (e). After Continue the URL stays `http://127.0.0.1:8080/` and never reaches `/projects`; the landing shows the alert "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')". The plan's assumption that the landing reads `complete` and navigates to `/projects` does not hold in the production build.
- **Cause (implementer's evidence):** the contracts package is emitted as CommonJS, and its production dynamic import exposes only `default`. The lazy chunk `apps/web/dist/scriba-web/browser/chunk-C1u1HVKo.js` ends with `export{chunk_LBEDIZWX_default as default}` and has no named exports. The loader in `apps/web/src/app/shell/contract-chunks.ts` line 12 returns that namespace unchanged. `apps/web/src/app/shell/landing.ts` line 49 reads `contract.SETUP_STATUS_ROUTE` as a named export (undefined). `apps/web/src/app/shell/api-client.ts` line 51 then throws the TypeError, and `landing.ts` lines 58 to 60 show it as the alert.
- **Same defect, already fixed in one place:** SAU-06's loader applies `return mod.default ?? mod;` (`apps/web/src/app/features/setup-auth/setup-contract.ts` line 26, comment lines 7 and 8). The shell loader (`shell/contract-chunks.ts`) does not, which matches the SHL-08 defect recorded for the user earlier.
- **Scope problem:** the fix belongs in `apps/web/src/app/shell/contract-chunks.ts`, which SAU-08's plan section 2 does not list, and assertion (e) must not be weakened. The reviser decides whether the fix moves into SAU-08's plan, into a new unit, or whether SAU-08 waits; a reply NAVIGATOR is expected if no correct plan fits the unit.
- **State of the branch:** `unit/SAU-08` holds commit `a1e1742` (`feat(SAU-08): add the token-guard gate tests`): G1 to G6 and both invariant files pass; mutations M1 to M3 applied and reverted cleanly. Steps 8b, 11 and 12 not run. The e2e edit to `e2e/specs/journey.e2e.ts` is left uncommitted in the worktree. The plan goes back to draft; a new reviser corrects it, and a new implementer continues from the branch commits.

## 2026-11-15 — TRG-04 — Navigator decision: O7, the drop mechanism and payload: option (b), Angular CDK drag and drop (Navigator session 79658fb02cd940728cc35b33237ed088)

- **Decision (Navigator, option b):** the picker is a `cdkDropList` whose `cdkDropListEnterPredicate` checks the dragged chip's type against the field's allowed kinds (any kind under P11; `style-profile` for a style picker). A chip is a `cdkDrag` whose `cdkDragData` is `{id: string, type: string}`. An accepted drop (`cdkDropListDropped`) appends in list mode with no duplicate ID, or replaces in scalar mode, and writes through the value model (P8). A refused drop shows the one-line reason (P16) and leaves `value` unchanged. Tests call the `cdkDropListDropped` output with a fake `CdkDragDrop`.
- **Downstream effect:** TRG-05's dev chip is a `cdkDrag` in the same `cdkDropListGroup` as the picker. GRR-12's side list is a `cdkDropList` of `cdkDrag` chips, connected to the picker lists inside the ngx-vflow nodes through `cdkDropListGroup` or connected IDs. GRR-15 (touch drop in Playwright) and GRR-17 (iPad drop in Safari) are real-gesture checks in their own units; this decision does not by itself make them pass.
- **Reason:** GRR-12 requires chips that work with mouse and touch. Native HTML drag and drop (a) is mouse-only by the browser spec, and the navigator states that its touch support in Safari is unreliable, which would make GRR-15 and GRR-17 need a second gesture. The Safari point was not verified in this session; it is the navigator's claim. CDK drag uses pointer events, one mechanism for mouse and touch. `@angular/cdk` 22.2.7 is already a direct dependency of apps/web (`apps/web/package.json`). Option (c) adds an exported API without solving the touch gap.
- **Checked by the orchestrator (`node_modules/@angular/cdk/types/drag-drop.d.ts`, 22.2.7):** `cdkDropListEnterPredicate`, `cdkDropListDropped`, `cdkDragData` and `CdkDropListGroup` (selector `cdkDropListGroup`) exist. There is no `DragDropGroup` class, so the navigator's term was corrected to `cdkDropListGroup`.
- **Navigator claims rejected or unverified:** (1) the plan on main did not yet record option (b) (commit f683ed7); a reviser must write section 7, steps 7 and 14, and the AC2b and AC2c rows. (2) GRR-15 and GRR-17 are satisfied by pointer events alone: not verified, no touch or iPad run was done.
- **Next:** a reviser updates plans/TRG-04.md to record this decision in section 7 and steps 7 and 14, then sets it to planned.

## 2026-11-15 — TRG-05 — Plan revision 3 (reviser, READY): correction of the PLAN DOES NOT WORK cause

- **Correction to the entry "PLAN DOES NOT WORK (implementer, branch head a4ef55c)" above.** The layout does not shift when the pointer passes the styleProfile picker. It shifts as soon as the drag starts. CDK runs every connected drop list's enter predicate once when a drag starts (`_startReceiving`, `@angular/cdk` drag-drop.mjs lines 2185-2191). The styleProfile picker's predicate `admits` (`entity-picker.ts`, lines 330-336 at c0d53a9) refuses a person chip and writes "A person cannot go here." into `<p class="reason">`, which was empty until then. That line moves the person select from y 805 to y 825. The drop target was measured before the drag, so the drop stayed in entityIds.
- **Evidence (reviser, a4ef55c, Chromium of Playwright 1.65.0, Node v26.13.0):** moving the pointer only to the "Entities" heading already shows the reason and puts the select at y 825. A straight drag to the select's centre, measured after the drag starts, sets person to ada and leaves entityIds empty (3 runs of 3). The original T2 still fails.
- **Settled in plan revision 3:** T2 keeps the real straight drag onto the person picker. Only the moment the target is measured changes: after the drag has started and two animation frames have passed. T2 gains (c) entityIds holds no chip after the drop and (d) no page error. The criterion text is unchanged. A detour, a synthetic drop, `dragTo`, and waiting on the refusal text are ruled out.
- **Observation for TRG-04's owner and for GRR-12, GRR-15 and GRR-17:** `admits` runs at drag start, and its reason line reflows the pickers below it, so CDK's cached rectangles for those lists go stale for the rest of the drag. TRG-05 does not change this.
- **Unit changes:** none. YAGNI: no criterion of TRG-05, TRG-07, TRG-13 or GRR-11 depends on the drag-start behaviour.
- The plan is `status: planned` (commit cea245a). The branch unit/TRG-05 continues from a4ef55c after a rebase onto main.

## 2026-11-15 — GRR-01 — Step 3 failed check: npm test on the rebased branch (orchestrator)

- The rebase of unit/GRR-01 onto main ae06185 is clean and gives head ce6019e (one commit). Lint passes; npm ci was run.
- `npm test` FAILS in apps/web: `apps/web/src/app/shell/landing.spec.ts` > "C1 routes by setup status and active project": expected '/' to be '/setup' (landing.spec.ts:68). The spec and landing.ts come from SHL-08 (commits c864e58 and d187c23, on main). GRR-01 does not change apps/web (`git diff main...unit/GRR-01 --stat -- apps/web` is empty).
- Not checked: whether the spec also fails on main (a run on main could not start: its node_modules does not resolve @codemirror/state). The failure is therefore not yet shown to be caused by GRR-01, and it is not shown to exist on main.
- Result: GRR-01 is held. The branch and worktree stay (`/Users/bbartolome/workspace/scriba-prototype-wt/GRR-01`). Build and patch-id check are not run. Criterion 5 still needs a decision (CI on a pushed main is not possible here).
- Open for the user: the SHL-08 failing spec on main (see also the SHL-08 defect noted in the handoff memory).
- **Correction (2026-11-15, after commit 1f1e234 on main; the text above is kept as written).** What was open is answered. The failure is a timing defect in the spec, not a defect in `shell/landing.ts` and not caused by GRR-01. `landing.spec.ts` C1 (and E1) wait on the landing's lazy load with `vi.waitFor` at its 1000 ms default. That load is a dynamic import of the setup-auth contract chunk, then the router's lazy load of the target route, and `whenStable()` does not track it. On a busy machine it takes longer than 1000 ms, so the first wait times out with "expected '/' to be '/setup'". The cited line `landing.spec.ts:68` is that first wait (`git show 1f1e234^:apps/web/src/app/shell/landing.spec.ts`, line 68). So the spec does fail on main, but intermittently and under load, not every run. Fix: commit 1f1e234 gives every wait a 5000 ms timeout and raises the two tests' own timeouts to 20000 and 10000 ms; no assertion is changed, removed or skipped. Reported by the subagent run: under load C1 failed 4 of 6 runs before the fix and passed 6 of 6 after; the full apps/web suite passes (325 of 325). "Same cause" for this GRR-01 failure rests on the identical test, assertion line and message; the GRR-01 branch itself was not re-run on the fixed spec. The "Open for the user" item above is closed by 1f1e234. GRR-01 stays held until the step 3 checks are repeated on a branch rebased onto 1f1e234 or later; that is not done.

## 2026-11-15 — AGL-05 — Step 3 failed check: pre-existing failure on main (orchestrator); not merged

- Code approval: not yet sought. Branch unit/AGL-05 at head 37946e6 (patch id 16da058c9490395540e5ff6411ea3897579c9ef9 for the code diff; the implementer reports COMPLETE, criteria C1 to C3 and S1 to S3 pass).
- Check failed: npm test (root) exits 1. The API workspace passes (91 files, 291 tests). The failure is apps/web src/app/shell/landing.spec.ts, test C1 "routes by setup status and active project": expected '/' to be '/setup'.
- Not caused by AGL-05: the branch does not change apps/web (git diff --name-only main...unit/AGL-05 lists no apps/web path; the apps/web tree equals main). The same spec fails on main when run alone (apps/web: npx vitest run src/app/shell/landing.spec.ts, 2 failed: C1 and E1). It passed in some full-suite runs earlier in this session and failed in others, so it is also intermittent.
- Same defect as noted for GRR-01 (SHL-08 landing spec, see the GRR-01 entry above). Step 3 of prompt.md requires all three checks to pass before a merge, so AGL-05 is not merged. Its branch and worktree are kept.
- Units on main from this session: MPR-08, AGL-03, AGL-10, AGL-04. The fifth unit is held by this failure.
- **Correction (2026-11-15, after commit 1f1e234 on main; the text above is kept as written).** Two statements above are wrong or misleading. (1) "The same spec fails on main when run alone (`npx vitest run src/app/shell/landing.spec.ts`, 2 failed: C1 and E1)" is a runner artifact, not a reproduction of the defect. The apps/web tests run through `npm test`, which is `ng test --watch=false` (the Angular unit-test builder, which initialises TestBed). The bare `npx vitest run` bypasses that builder, so every spec fails there regardless of its content: landing.spec.ts fails both tests with "Need to call TestBed.initTestEnvironment() first" (re-run on main at 1f1e234, where the spec is already fixed, with the same result), and app-nav.spec.ts fails 9 of 9 with "window is not defined". The "2 failed: C1 and E1" were that error, not the assertion failure seen in the full-suite run. (2) "Pre-existing failure on main" is true only in the sense that the flaky spec was already on main. The real cause, found afterwards: C1 and E1 wait on a lazy load with `vi.waitFor` at its 1000 ms default, and under CPU load it times out intermittently ("expected '/' to be '/setup'"). That matches the entry's own observation that the spec passed in some full-suite runs and failed in others. Still true: AGL-05 does not cause it, and it is the same defect as the GRR-01 entry (see the correction there). Fix: commit 1f1e234 (5000 ms wait timeouts, test timeouts 20000 and 10000 ms, no assertion changed). Reported by the subagent run: C1 failed 4 of 6 runs under load before the fix and passed 6 of 6 after; the full apps/web suite passes (325 of 325). AGL-05 is still not merged: the cause of its hold is fixed on main, but the three step 3 checks have not been repeated on a branch rebased onto 1f1e234 or later (head 37946e6 predates it); that is not done.

## 2026-11-16 — PST-34 — Navigator decision OP-B: an outside change does not reload the editor on tablet and desktop (orchestrator record)

- **Question (OP-B in plans/PST-34.md, reported by the reviser as NAVIGATOR):** on tablet and desktop, should a `files-changed` event or a reconcile tick naming the open file reload the editor from disk?
- **Decision: option (a), no reload.** The editor keeps the text it loaded. A save against a changed file is refused with `PROJECT_WRITE_CONFLICT` and shows the stale-base warning through the conflict status line and the alert (SHL-14 D6 and D8), and the author's text is kept. Phone is unchanged.
- **Reason (the scope reason):** option (b) must tell the author's own save from an outside change, because every successful write publishes `files-changed` (`units/PST-06-file-api-core.md` line 25). That forces a text comparison and a timing window (flush-then-prompt with a stale base, `plans/PST-34.md` line 155) that the spec does not require. Option (c) adds a notice and a Reload button that no unit names. The no-text-loss reason does not separate the options, because (b) also never discards text. SHL-14 D7 (`plans/SHL-14.md` line 32) is scoped to the conflict state and does not forbid (b); it is cited only for the conflict warning.
- **Effects:** on tablet and desktop, after an outside change the editor keeps the old text until the file is reopened, while the tree and the version-history list refresh. PST-21 scope is unchanged. PST-22 demo step 4 passes; its visible confirmation on tablet and desktop is the refreshed list and tree. SHL-19 is unaffected: its demo step 2 is the Shell draft split view, not the Files page.
- **Navigator session:** c793ffa3788c475db495b9c044e09fc7. The first rationale (that (b) and (c) contradict SHL-14 D7) was retracted after challenge. Two carry-forward lines were wrong and were corrected: the PST-21 claim that the preview updates (no preview exists on tablet and desktop, `plans/PST-34.md` PC2), and the PST-22 claim that blocked_by is PST-21 only (`units/PST-22-review-gate.md` line 7 lists six units).

## 2026-11-16 — TRG-11 — Navigator decision (session `bdff3d67d65d4a559466405951cab519`, option A): a GET may publish `catalog-changed` when its re-scan finds a host-side change

- **Decision (Navigator, option A):** "GET never mutates" (`modules/tool-registry.md` line 42; `units/README.md` line 131) and "GETs are side-effect free" (`units/TRG-09-tool-registry-read-enable.md` line 26) mean that the request changes no file and no stored state. A read may publish `tool-registry/catalog-changed` when its user-pack re-scan (`apps/api/src/modules/tool-registry/catalog.service.ts`, `refresh()`, lines 158 to 161) finds a change made host-side. The in-memory scan is a derived cache of the files. The change was made outside the GET, so the GET reports it and does not make it.
- **Reason:** (1) The module's own requirements: host-side user-pack edits show up without a restart (`units/TRG-06-pack-loader-catalog.md` line 15, item 29), and open views refresh after changes (`units/TRG-10-save-delete-catalog-changed.md` line 15, item 51). With "no watcher" (TRG-06 Decisions, line 20), the re-scan on read is the only detection mechanism and `catalog-changed` the only notification channel. (2) The invariant sweep's documented exception, `apps/api/test/invariant-sweep.ts` `EVENT_ALLOWLIST` (lines 155 to 166), allows exactly this one event on a GET, citing TRG-06 line 20 and TRG-10 line 21. (3) Option B would break done criteria: TRG-10 criterion 4 ("`catalog-changed` arrives on `/events` after save, delete, toggle and a host-side file add", line 27) has no other trigger.
- **Consequence:** the module wording stays (no edit to `modules/tool-registry.md`). TRG-06 and TRG-10 stay `done`, with no new unit. TRG-11 criterion 1 is unblocked: TRG-09 criterion 4 holds on `main` as tested (T4 checks that files do not change; the allowed event is the documented exception). `plans/TRG-11.md` stands as committed at `6e88616`; a reviser restates its open point 5 as decided, and step 7's sentence is written under option A. This entry closes the "not yet confirmed" note of the 2026-11-16 TRG-10 code review (line 4920).

TRG-14 line 16: the detail's editor tab reads `GET …/tools/:name/user` for an invalid user copy. TRG-16: a Decisions bullet that the Try tab is hidden on an invalid row (or shows `TOOL_INVALID`). TRG-15 and TRG-17: not affected by this decision. Point 1 (option b) and point 3 (every origin) stay settled.

## 2026-11-16 — AGL-17 — implement: PLAN DOES NOT WORK (orchestrator record)

- **Report (Haiku implementer, worktree `scriba-prototype-wt/AGL-17`, branch `unit/AGL-17` at `868e059`, no commits made):** PLAN DOES NOT WORK.
- **Step:** section 4.3, step 1 (create `apps/api/test/agent-loop-grounding-wiring.test.ts`), specifically test C1's assertion in section 5, row C1. The plan says the pending change's `contentHash` must equal `sha256:` plus the SHA-256 of the sentence and newline. The implementer stopped before it wrote any file.
- **Cause:** the contract has no such field. `packages/contracts/src/project-store/pending.ts`, `pendingChangeSchema` (lines 36 to 56), has no `contentHash`. - **Smaller mismatch in the same test:** the plan finds the change by `path`. The contract field is `targetPath` (`pending.ts` line 40). `path` is the field of the propose input (line 77), not of the listed change.
- **Checked by the implementer and consistent with the code:** `grounding-engine.ts` check and `GroundingFailure` (lines 40 to 137), `tool-run.ts` dispatch catch (lines 164 to 186), `agent-run.ts` finish (388 to 404) and flushWrites (408 to 439), `transcript-reader.ts` `runOf` default branch (206 to 208), `runStateOfTranscript` (line 121), `AGENT_GROUNDING_ROUTE`, the event schemas, and `groundingRequestSchema`.
- **Requested correction (from the report, for the reviser to check):** revise section 5, row C1, so that it checks the grounding-result `contentHash` (or the artefact's `contentHash`) against the SHA-256 of the sentence and newline, and finds the pending change by `targetPath`.

## 2026-11-16 — AGL-19 — PLAN DOES NOT WORK (implementer, plan section 4.4, T2 step 8)

- **Branch:** `unit/AGL-19`, commit d0d88c1 (plan steps 1 to 4: the chapter 4 grounding draft and its outline line). Worktree `scriba-prototype-wt/AGL-19`.

- **Cause:** the plan assumes that the route answers `null` when no run is active. It does not. `apps/api/src/modules/agent-loop/agent-runs.service.ts` lines 182 to 195 (`current()`) return the state of the project's last run, active or ended. `null` is returned only when the project has never had a run. ## 2026-11-17 — SAU-18 — Owner decision: accept and document the peer-header risk (no code change)

- **Decision (owner, recorded by the orchestrator):** accept the risk of the peer rule in `apps/api/src/modules/setup-auth/setup-auth.guard.ts` and document it. The guard trusts the `tailscale-user-login` header only from a loopback peer (`SERVE_PEERS`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1`, at `:43`). The SAU-18 code is not changed.
- **The risk, as the owner accepted it:** any process inside the scriba network namespace can send that header from a loopback peer and get `{via:'tailnet', login}` for any login. A request from outside the namespace cannot forge it, because its peer is not loopback.
- **Alternatives not chosen:** (a) a shared secret between Tailscale Serve and the API, sent with the header; (b) a whois check against the tailnet for each request; (c) an unpublished Serve listener that only Serve can reach. The design of `modules/setup-auth.md` (the peer-address check, with the dedicated Serve listener as the named fallback) stands unchanged.
- **Reason:** the owner's decision. The owner gave no reason in the record. The trust boundary that the accepted design relies on is the scriba network namespace.
- **Follow-up for the record:** `units/SAU-22-guard-dev-mode.md` and the `devAuth` skip do not change this rule (D17 in `plans/SAU-18.md`). SAU-21 keeps the Serve peer check as its criterion, and the fallback is not built.

## 2026-11-17 — GRR-09 — PLAN DOES NOT WORK (implementer, step 7)

- **Branch and worktree:** `unit/GRR-09` at 001bace (= main at that commit), worktree `scriba-prototype-wt/GRR-09`. The implementer made no commit. Its uncommitted work is kept in that worktree: `apps/web/src/app/app.routes.ts` (step 6 entry, done) and the new folder `apps/web/src/app/features/graph-runner/` (`graph-runner.routes.ts`, `canvas-placeholder-page.ts`, `graph-runner-contract.ts`, `graph-runner-contract.spec.ts`, `graph-list-page.ts`, `graph-list-page.spec.ts`).
- **Report:** steps 0 to 4 and 6 are done, step 7 (page spec) fails on AC1 and AC2. Test results: `graph-runner-contract.spec.ts` 6 of 6 passed (step 2, X3); `graph-list-page.spec.ts` 2 passed and 7 failed (C2.2 and X2 pass; C1.1 to C1.5, C2.1 and X1 fail by timeout, because the rows never render). Steps 8 to 10 were not run.
- **Cause, as the implementer reports it (not yet verified by the orchestrator):** plan assumption A5 is wrong. Step 5 has the page take its project id from `ActiveProjectSignal.projectId()` in the constructor. That signal (`apps/web/src/app/shell/project-scope.ts`, lines 75 to 85, Shell-owned) gets its value from the router snapshot only when the root service is built, then updates on `NavigationEnd`. The page is created before `NavigationEnd`, so `projectId()` is `''` at construction. `readOf` returns EMPTY for `''`, so no GET is sent. A debug dump after navigating to `/projects/p1/graphs` showed only `GET /api/project-store/active` and `GET /api/project-store/projects`; none of the graph-runner reads was sent.
- **Difference from the plan, needed to run any web test:** a fresh worktree has no `packages/contracts/dist`, so the web specs cannot resolve `@bbartolome/scriba-contracts/*`. The implementer ran `npm run build -w @bbartolome/scriba-contracts` (exit 0; the output is gitignored). The plan does not list this step.
- **Suggested fix (the implementer's suggestion; the reviser decides):** take the project id from the page's own route (for example the `projectId` param of `ActivatedRoute.snapshot.pathFromRoot`), or wait for `NavigationEnd` before the first read. Then rerun steps 7 to 10.
- **Route taken (orchestrator):** the plan goes back to `status: draft`. A new Opus reviser corrects it. When it is `planned` again, a new implementer continues from the commits of `unit/GRR-09` (the uncommitted work stays in its worktree and must not be discarded).
